label: input i at positions 2-6 of the original phase, gated by the first token (z/x/f/n strongest)
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, and only when the input token is i (100% of activations). It never fires at t=0 or 1, or in the delimiter or copy phases. It peaks at t=3-4 and is rare after t=6. Only about 24% of i inputs at t>=2 fire, and the context sets which ones. The first original token matters most: sequences starting with z, x, f or n fire about 3x as often and give the largest activations (top examples look like z n f f [i], f n n 1 [i]). Starting with s, l, c or o gives a moderate rate. Having n/f/x/z earlier in the prefix also helps. A first occurrence of i fires much more than a repeated one, though repeats occasionally fire. The leftover activations (about 18% of mass) are mostly weak and fall in sequences with other first tokens; the false positives are i inputs after one of the listed first tokens where the feature stays silent. Dev F1 is 0.72 and mass recall 0.82.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, -, h, b, a, x; least: 0, 2, f, <DEL>) and the first original token (most: z, f, x, n, c, s; least: b, h, u, i); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=3, t=5.
